text: Hi, I’m Meher Didi, and this is my kitchen. Tonight families order party boxes until midnight. If a box comes late or cold, a party goes without food.
Nobody will tell you what good enough means tonight.. Our name is on every box. Your team decides what good enough means, tests it and changes it. At midnight, you judge the night.
One party box for the whole night. Three foods. Pick what you think works. Tonight will tell us.
Tonight your team sets the bar. A bar is like the bar in a high jump: the line you aim to get over. First, read what our customers say.
What does good enough mean tonight?. Our bar is what every box should manage tonight. There is no right answer.
Before the real orders, let’s try one practice order together. Nothing counts yet.
Chef 1, you’re Prep. Tap the chopping board until every dot is filled.
Chef 2, you’re Cook. Tap an empty burner to start cooking.
Watch the ring fill up. That’s the food cooking.
It’s ready! Chef 2, tap the food. In the real rush, food left too long burns.
Chef 3, you’re Pack. Tap each food into the box, then tap Seal and label.
Chef 4, you’re Dispatch. Tap Send to give the box to a rider.
That’s the whole trip: Prep, Cook, Pack, Dispatch. The bar under each station shows how many orders wait there. If a station glows gold, it’s falling behind, and anyone can tap HELP to jump in.
Here come the real orders! Look after your own station, and keep an eye on the others.
Far side is slow tonight. Twenty-four minutes each way.
First tries are for learning. Let’s look at what really happened.
Your first box met real orders.
Bad news, team. Six of our riders are heading home, family stuff. We are down to six. We will ride safe, not fast.
How many riders are free now?. Everyone except Chef 4 answers, using only what Chef 4 told you, so the whole team plans with the same facts.
There is no one right answer. Pick a plan you can explain.
What do families need to hear?. They’re getting ready for a party. Pick only what they need, in words they understand.
What do riders need to know?. They’re on a scooter, about to leave. Pick what they need to do the job.
Ninety minutes to midnight. Same jobs, new plan, new bar. Let’s see how it works.
One change, and the clue that shows why.
Good enough changed tonight because the night changed. Where else is that true?
Hmm. Would your best look the same for a sandcastle at the beach and a real house?
Now: judges at a baking contest. What would good enough be here? Say it out loud together.
By your own bar, how did the night go?. Pass = it reached your bar. Fail = it didn’t.
Finish this sentence together, out loud:.
Thanks, team. Everyone got home safe. Some boxes were late, and you told people the truth.
Our name was on every box tonight. You decided what that meant.
You know these customers. You decide.
Thanks, team. Safe, and before midnight.
Chef 2, you’re running Prep too. Tap the chopping board until every dot is filled.
Every line passed. What does that tell you?. Was it easy because the kitchen did well, or because the bar was low?
An honest mark shows what to change.
Why do you think those lines failed?.
Knowing why helps you change the right thing.
We told people the real time
